parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence: Section 164 was struck down (2019, upheld 2021) and deleted in 2026; prosecutions were rare and police were reported not to target. Courts have actively worked FOR trans people — 2017 rulings compelled gender recognition and produced an actual ID card, and constitutional 'sex' interpretation was broadened. No documented border, facility, custody or care exposure appears, and no trans-directed violence is recorded (though the newest violence data is 2011, so silence proves little). Weighing against: Section 167 survives, tolerance is middling (50% neighbour measure, 2021, measuring homosexuality not trans identity), societal discrimination and mixed official rhetoric persist, precedents implement unsatisfactorily, and no administrative recognition route exists (a resident gap, not visitor exposure). Court relief functions but slowly. Net: functioning protection with real social friction and thin recent data — Reduced Risk, mid-tier.
